text:
alex: FYI NimbusHealth POC—customer hit consistent 429s during a mixed embeddings + rerank job. Repro when they run 4 workers, ~20s in. Need quick triage so sales doesn't lose momentum.

toni: Can they share one full response (headers + body) and a failing request id? Also which API endpoints were used (embeddings vs /chat/complete/rerank)?

alex: They used embeddings then a rerank call per doc. Sample header from their capture: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1200
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1725004500
X-Request-ID: req_0a1b2c3d` Body: `{"error":"rate limit exceeded"}`. They also sent 3x retries with no backoff.

rohit: That limit looks like minute token cap. But rerank calls can consume a lot of tokens if context is large. Do we have their tenant config? @maria can you check if rerank and embeddings share the same per-route bucket?

maria: Checking 10: tenant nimbus-prod currently has: tenant_quota=10000/min, route_overrides: embeddings->2000/min, rerank->500/min (legacy mapping). That rerank bucket is definitely too small for their test. Also noticed their trial key was flagged for per-route isolation which prevents spillover.

ops-bot: Auto-alert: tenant nimbus state=THROTTLED; rerank route softcap reached (500/min). Suggested action: temporary rerank bump +800 for 1 hour.

toni: Good catch. Two-step remediation: (1) temp bump so they can finish the POC run; (2) longitudinal fix: either merge rerank into shared bucket for trials or increase default rerank override.

alex: Could we also ask them to attach a sample X-Request-ID for a failed rerank and the client timeline? Need to verify whether retries happened before Reset or after.

rohit: Also flag on-client changes: reduce rerank context length, paginate candidates, or run rerank with lower temperature (irrelevant for token cost but sometimes clients do extra calls). Main thing: smaller prompt context and increase batching for embeddings only.

maria: I pushed the temp bump to rerank +800/min for 1 hour and notified the customer. I also attached a link to recommended client config in the message: https://console.redwood.ai/docs/poc-guides/rerank-throttle.

alex: Customer tested immediately and reports 429s persisted for 2 of 8 runs. They posted `X-Request-ID: req_0d4e5f6a` and timings show they retried after 0s and 1s.

toni: Those immediate retries explain the burst. Need to add recommended exponential backoff and capped retries in the POC template. For now, tell them to add 500ms jitter and cap at 3 retries.

rohit: Long term infra follow-ups: (a) ensure any per-route override created during onboarding is sized relative to tenant_quota; (b) console should surface per-route exhaustion as a first-class metric; (c) consider a graceful 429 header that includes suggested retry-after and current per-route remaining tokens to help clients self-throttle.

maria: Filed infra ticket INFRA-4127 for provisioning mismatch and UX ticket UX-2098 to surface per-route pressure.

ops-bot: Note: temp bump will expire at 1725007921.

alex: After bump + customer backoff changes, they completed a 12-minute run with no further 429s. Sales says POC still green.

toni: Follow-ups for presales docs: add a one-paragraph checklist for sales to validate before demos: expected tokens/min for common workloads, how to capture X-Request-ID, and to request a short dry-run under support supervision.

rohit: Also add a sample `curl -v` snippet for clients to paste: ``curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"input":["..."],"batch_size":8}' -v`` Include note to include the X-Request-ID header we send back.

alex: Great. I'm updating the POC checklist and emailing sales + support with the runbook. Customer happy for now. :white_check_mark:
